import Mathlib

/-!
# Eulerian trails in finite multigraphs and the Euler parity theorem

This file gives a small, self-contained formalization of *Eulerian trails* in finite
multigraphs and proves the classical **Euler parity theorem**: in any graph carrying an
Eulerian trail, at most two vertices have odd degree, and if the trail is closed
(its start and end vertices coincide) then every vertex has even degree.

## Main definitions

* `Multigraph nV nE` : a finite multigraph on vertex set `Fin nV` with edge set `Fin nE`,
  given by two endpoint maps `endpt₁, endpt₂ : Fin nE → Fin nV`.  A loop is an edge with
  `endpt₁ e = endpt₂ e`; it contributes `2` to the degree of its vertex (the standard
  convention).
* `Multigraph.degree G v` : the degree of `v`, the number of edge–endpoint incidences at
  `v` (so `endpt₁`-incidences plus `endpt₂`-incidences).
* `EulerianTrail G` : a walk that uses every edge exactly once.  It consists of a sequence
  of `nE + 1` vertices, a permutation `edgePerm` of the edges giving the order in which the
  edges are traversed, and a proof `connects` that the `i`-th traversed edge joins the
  `i`-th and `(i+1)`-st vertex of the walk.
* `EulerianTrail.visitCount T v` : how many of the `nE + 1` positions of the walk equal `v`.

## Main results

* `EulerianTrail.degree_add_indicators` : the local counting identity
  `degree v + startIndicator v + endIndicator v = 2 * visitCount v`.
* `EulerianTrail.odd_degree_mem` : a vertex of odd degree must be the start or end vertex.
* `EulerianTrail.odd_degree_vertices_le_two` : at most two vertices have odd degree.
* `EulerianTrail.even_degree_of_closed` : in a closed trail every vertex has even degree.
-/

namespace Catalog.Euler

open Finset

/-- A finite multigraph on vertices `Fin nV` and edges `Fin nE`, described by its two
endpoint maps.  Edges are undirected; the order of the two endpoints is irrelevant. -/
structure Multigraph (nV nE : ℕ) where
  /-- First endpoint of an edge. -/
  endpt₁ : Fin nE → Fin nV
  /-- Second endpoint of an edge. -/
  endpt₂ : Fin nE → Fin nV

variable {nV nE : ℕ}

/-- The degree of a vertex `v`: the number of edge–endpoint incidences at `v`.  Each edge
contributes `1` for each of its two endpoints equal to `v`, so a loop at `v` contributes
`2`. -/
def Multigraph.degree (G : Multigraph nV nE) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  (univ.filter (fun e => G.endpt₁ e = v)).card +
    (univ.filter (fun e => G.endpt₂ e = v)).card

/-- An Eulerian trail of `G`: a walk through `nE + 1` vertices that traverses every edge
exactly once, in the order given by the permutation `edgePerm`. -/
structure EulerianTrail (G : Multigraph nV nE) where
  /-- The vertices visited by the walk, in order. -/
  vertices : Fin (nE + 1) → Fin nV
  /-- The order in which the edges are traversed. -/
  edgePerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin nE)
  /-- The `i`-th traversed edge joins the `i`-th and `(i+1)`-st walk vertices. -/
  connects : ∀ i : Fin nE,
    let e := edgePerm i
    (G.endpt₁ e = vertices i.castSucc ∧ G.endpt₂ e = vertices i.succ) ∨
      (G.endpt₁ e = vertices i.succ ∧ G.endpt₂ e = vertices i.castSucc)

namespace EulerianTrail

variable {G : Multigraph nV nE}

/-- The first vertex of the walk. -/
def startVertex (T : EulerianTrail G) : Fin nV := T.vertices 0

/-- The last vertex of the walk. -/
def endVertex (T : EulerianTrail G) : Fin nV := T.vertices (Fin.last nE)

/-- The number of positions of the walk that equal `v`. -/
def visitCount (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  (univ.filter (fun j : Fin (nE + 1) => T.vertices j = v)).card

/-- Indicator (`0`/`1`) of whether `v` is the start vertex of the walk. -/
def startIndicator (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  if T.startVertex = v then 1 else 0

/-- Indicator (`0`/`1`) of whether `v` is the end vertex of the walk. -/
def endIndicator (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  if T.endVertex = v then 1 else 0

/-- **Local counting identity.**  For every vertex `v`, the degree of `v` plus the
start/end indicators equals twice the number of times the walk visits `v`.  Each interior
visit accounts for two incident edges, while a visit at the start or end leaves one
unmatched incidence. -/
theorem degree_add_indicators (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) :
    G.degree v + T.startIndicator v + T.endIndicator v = 2 * T.visitCount v := by
  -- Let `F j := if T.vertices j = v then 1 else 0`.
  set F : Fin (nE + 1) → ℕ := fun j => if T.vertices j = v then 1 else 0;
  -- By definition of $F$, we can rewrite the sums in terms of $F$.
  have h_sums : (∑ x : Fin nE, (if G.endpt₁ x = v then 1 else 0)) + (∑ x : Fin nE, (if G.endpt₂ x = v then 1 else 0)) = (∑ i : Fin nE, F (Fin.castSucc i)) + (∑ i : Fin nE, F (Fin.succ i)) := by
    have h_sums : ∀ i : Fin nE, (if G.endpt₁ (T.edgePerm i) = v then 1 else 0) + (if G.endpt₂ (T.edgePerm i) = v then 1 else 0) = F (Fin.castSucc i) + F (Fin.succ i) := by
      intro i; rcases T.connects i with h | h <;> simp +decide [ h ] ;
      · rfl;
      · grind;
    rw [ ← Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib ];
    rw [ ← Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i hi => h_sums i, Equiv.sum_comp T.edgePerm fun i => ( if G.endpt₁ i = v then 1 else 0 ) + if G.endpt₂ i = v then 1 else 0 ];
  -- By definition of $F$, we can rewrite the sums in terms of $F$ and simplify.
  have h_sums_simplified : (∑ i : Fin nE, F (Fin.castSucc i)) + (∑ i : Fin nE, F (Fin.succ i)) + F 0 + F (Fin.last nE) = 2 * (∑ j : Fin (nE + 1), F j) := by
    have := Fin.sum_univ_castSucc F; have := Fin.sum_univ_succ F; norm_num at *; linarith;
  unfold Multigraph.degree EulerianTrail.startIndicator EulerianTrail.endIndicator EulerianTrail.visitCount; aesop;

/-- The degree of `v` has the same parity as the sum of the start/end indicators at `v`. -/
theorem degree_mod_two (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) :
    G.degree v % 2 = (T.startIndicator v + T.endIndicator v) % 2 := by
  have h1 := degree_add_indicators T v; have h2 := G.degree v; simp_all +arith +decide; omega;

/-- A vertex of odd degree must be the start or the end vertex of the trail. -/
theorem odd_degree_mem (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) (h : G.degree v % 2 = 1) :
    v = T.startVertex ∨ v = T.endVertex := by
  contrapose! h;
  rw [ EulerianTrail.degree_mod_two ];
  unfold startIndicator endIndicator
  rw [if_neg h.1.symm, if_neg h.2.symm]
  decide

/-- **Euler parity theorem.**  At most two vertices have odd degree in a graph that
carries an Eulerian trail. -/
theorem odd_degree_vertices_le_two (T : EulerianTrail G) :
    (univ.filter (fun v => G.degree v % 2 = 1)).card ≤ 2 := by
  -- By `odd_degree_mem`, every odd-degree vertex must be either the start or end vertex of the trail.
  have h_odd_degree : ∀ v : Fin nV, G.degree v % 2 = 1 → v ∈ ({T.startVertex, T.endVertex} : Finset (Fin nV)) := by
    exact fun v hv => by simpa using odd_degree_mem T v hv;
  exact le_trans ( Finset.card_le_card fun v hv => h_odd_degree v <| Finset.mem_filter.mp hv |>.2 ) ( Finset.card_insert_le _ _ )

/-
**Closed-trail corollary.**  If the Eulerian trail is closed (start equals end), then
every vertex has even degree.
-/
theorem even_degree_of_closed (T : EulerianTrail G)
    (h : T.startVertex = T.endVertex) (v : Fin nV) :
    Even (G.degree v) := by
  -- From `h : T.startVertex = T.endVertex`, the indicators agree: `T.startIndicator v = T.endIndicator v`.
  have h_indicator_eq : T.startIndicator v = T.endIndicator v := by
    unfold EulerianTrail.startIndicator EulerianTrail.endIndicator; aesop;
  grind +suggestions

end EulerianTrail

end Catalog.Euler

# A categorical notion of "mutation" via adjunctions

This small bridge file formalizes a *modest* category-theoretic notion of mutation between two
algebraic settings: a **pair of categories together with an adjunction** between them.  The data
is exactly a left adjoint `toTarget : Source ⥤ Target` and a right adjoint `toSource` together
with the adjunction `toTarget ⊣ toSource`.  Intuitively the adjunction lets one "mutate" objects
back and forth (free construction one way, forgetful construction the other) while preserving the
universal hom-set correspondence.

We instantiate this on two concrete families already supported by Mathlib:

* `monoidMutation`: the free–forgetful adjunction `Type ⇄ MonCat`,
* `quiverCategoryMutation`: the free-category–forgetful adjunction `Quiv ⇄ Cat`.

This deliberately avoids any speculative "Morita-equivalence iff model-category-equivalence"
statement; everything here is backed by definitions and adjunctions present in Mathlib.
-/

import Mathlib

open CategoryTheory

namespace CategoryMutationBridge

/-- A **categorical mutation** is a pair of categories `Source` and `Target` related by an
adjunction `toTarget ⊣ toSource`.  The left adjoint `toTarget` plays the role of a free/synthesis
construction and the right adjoint `toSource` the role of a forgetful/analysis construction. -/
structure CategoryMutation where
  /-- The "source" category. -/
  Source : Type*
  [instSource : Category Source]
  /-- The "target" category. -/
  Target : Type*
  [instTarget : Category Target]
  /-- The left adjoint (free / synthesis direction). -/
  toTarget : Source ⥤ Target
  /-- The right adjoint (forgetful / analysis direction). -/
  toSource : Target ⥤ Source
  /-- The witnessing adjunction. -/
  adj : toTarget ⊣ toSource

attribute [instance] CategoryMutation.instSource CategoryMutation.instTarget

namespace CategoryMutation

/-- The hom-set correspondence of a categorical mutation: morphisms out of a "freely synthesized"
object `toTarget.obj x` correspond naturally to morphisms into the "forgotten" object
`toSource.obj y`.  This is the defining universal property of the adjunction. -/
noncomputable def homCorrespondence (M : CategoryMutation) (x : M.Source) (y : M.Target) :
    (M.toTarget.obj x ⟶ y) ≃ (x ⟶ M.toSource.obj y) :=
  M.adj.homEquiv x y

end CategoryMutation

/-- **Example.** The free–forgetful adjunction between plain types and monoids, viewed as a
categorical mutation `Type ⇄ MonCat`. -/
noncomputable def monoidMutation : CategoryMutation where
  Source := Type
  Target := MonCat
  toTarget := MonCat.free
  toSource := forget MonCat
  adj := MonCat.adj

/-- **Example.** The free-category–forgetful adjunction between quivers and categories, viewed as
a categorical mutation `Quiv ⇄ Cat`. -/
noncomputable def quiverCategoryMutation : CategoryMutation where
  Source := Quiv
  Target := Cat
  toTarget := Cat.free
  toSource := Quiv.forget
  adj := Quiv.adj

end CategoryMutationBridge

  (an `ℕ`-valued "handshake along the trail" identity),
* the equivalent interior form `degree v = 2 * interiorCount v + startIndicator v + endIndicator v`
  (for graphs with at least one edge),
* the parity consequence `Even (degree v)` for every vertex that is neither the start nor the
  end of the trail, and
* the main theorem `odd_degree_vertices_le_two`: the set of odd-degree vertices has cardinality
  at most `2`.

A multigraph here is a finite vertex set `Fin nV`, a finite edge set `Fin nE`, and for each edge
an ordered pair of endpoints (orientation is irrelevant for degrees; loops and parallel edges are
allowed). An Eulerian trail is a vertex sequence `Fin (nE + 1) → Fin nV`, a permutation of the
edges, and a proof that the `i`-th permuted edge connects the `i`-th and `(i+1)`-th vertices.
-/

import Mathlib

open Finset BigOperators

namespace EulerianTrail

/-- The number of occurrences of `v` in the two-element multiset `{a, b}`. -/
theorem count_pair {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (a b v : α) :
    Multiset.count v ({a, b} : Multiset α) = (if a = v then 1 else 0) + (if b = v then 1 else 0) := by
  simp [Multiset.insert_eq_cons, Multiset.count_cons]
  rcases eq_or_ne a v with h | h <;> rcases eq_or_ne b v with h2 | h2 <;>
    simp_all [eq_comm]

/-- A finite multigraph: a vertex set `Fin nV`, an edge set `Fin nE`, and for each edge an
ordered pair of endpoints.  Orientation is irrelevant for the degree, and both loops (the two
endpoints coincide) and parallel edges are allowed. -/
structure Multigraph where
  /-- Number of vertices. -/
  nV : ℕ
  /-- Number of edges. -/
  nE : ℕ
  /-- The two endpoints of each edge. -/
  ends : Fin nE → Fin nV × Fin nV

namespace Multigraph

variable (G : Multigraph)

/-- The endpoints of edge `e`, packaged as a multiset of size two (so a loop contributes its
endpoint twice). -/
def edgeMultiset (e : Fin G.nE) : Multiset (Fin G.nV) := {(G.ends e).1, (G.ends e).2}

/-- The **degree** of a vertex: the number of edge-endpoints incident to it, where a loop counts
twice. -/
def degree (v : Fin G.nV) : ℕ := ∑ e : Fin G.nE, Multiset.count v (G.edgeMultiset e)

/-- An **Eulerian trail** in `G`: a vertex sequence `walk` visiting `nE + 1` vertices, a
permutation `perm` of the edges, and a proof that the `i`-th permuted edge connects the `i`-th and
`(i+1)`-th vertices of the sequence. -/
structure EulerTrail (G : Multigraph) where
  /-- The sequence of visited vertices. -/
  walk : Fin (G.nE + 1) → Fin G.nV
  /-- The order in which the edges are traversed. -/
  perm : Equiv.Perm (Fin G.nE)
  /-- The `i`-th traversed edge connects the `i`-th and `(i+1)`-th vertices. -/
  connects : ∀ i : Fin G.nE,
    G.edgeMultiset (perm i) = {walk i.castSucc, walk i.succ}

namespace EulerTrail

variable {G}

/-- The start vertex of the trail. -/
def startVertex (T : EulerTrail G) : Fin G.nV := T.walk 0

/-- The end vertex of the trail. -/
def endVertex (T : EulerTrail G) : Fin G.nV := T.walk (Fin.last G.nE)

/-- `1` if the trail starts at `v`, else `0`. -/
def startIndicator (T : EulerTrail G) (v : Fin G.nV) : ℕ := if T.walk 0 = v then 1 else 0

/-- `1` if the trail ends at `v`, else `0`. -/
def endIndicator (T : EulerTrail G) (v : Fin G.nV) : ℕ :=
  if T.walk (Fin.last G.nE) = v then 1 else 0

/-- The total number of positions in the walk at which the vertex `v` appears. -/
def posCount (T : EulerTrail G) (v : Fin G.nV) : ℕ :=
  ∑ j : Fin (G.nE + 1), if T.walk j = v then 1 else 0

/-- The number of **interior** positions (neither the first nor the last) at which `v` appears. -/
def interiorCount (T : EulerTrail G) (v : Fin G.nV) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter
    (fun j : Fin (G.nE + 1) => j ≠ 0 ∧ j ≠ Fin.last G.nE ∧ T.walk j = v)).card

/-- The degree of `v` equals the number of trail-steps at which `v` is an endpoint of the
traversed edge, counted with multiplicity at both ends of each step. -/
theorem degree_eq_walk_sum (T : EulerTrail G) (v : Fin G.nV) :
    G.degree v = ∑ i : Fin G.nE,
      ((if T.walk i.castSucc = v then 1 else 0) + (if T.walk i.succ = v then 1 else 0)) := by
  convert ( Equiv.sum_comp T.perm ( fun e => Multiset.count v ( G.edgeMultiset e ) ) ).symm using 2;
  rw [ T.connects, EulerianTrail.count_pair ]

/-- **Incidence-count identity** (additive `ℕ` form): summing the endpoint incidences of `v`
along the trail counts every interior occurrence twice and each of the two endpoint occurrences
once, giving `degree v + startIndicator v + endIndicator v = 2 * posCount v`. -/
theorem degree_add_indicators (T : EulerTrail G) (v : Fin G.nV) :
    G.degree v + T.startIndicator v + T.endIndicator v = 2 * T.posCount v := by
  rw [ EulerTrail.degree_eq_walk_sum T v ];
  simp +decide only [sum_add_distrib, startIndicator, endIndicator, posCount];
  have := Fin.sum_univ_castSucc ( fun x => if T.walk x = v then 1 else 0 ) ; have := Fin.sum_univ_succ ( fun x => if T.walk x = v then 1 else 0 ) ; simp_all +decide [ two_mul ] ;
  grind

/-- For a graph with at least one edge, the total occurrence count splits into the interior count
plus the two endpoint indicators. -/
theorem posCount_eq_interior (T : EulerTrail G) (hE : 1 ≤ G.nE) (v : Fin G.nV) :
    T.posCount v = T.interiorCount v + T.startIndicator v + T.endIndicator v := by
  unfold EulerTrail.posCount EulerTrail.startIndicator EulerTrail.endIndicator EulerTrail.interiorCount;
  rw [ Finset.sum_eq_sum_diff_singleton_add ( Finset.mem_univ 0 ), Finset.sum_eq_sum_diff_singleton_add ( Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨ Finset.mem_univ ( Fin.last _ ), ?_ ⟩ ) ];
  · simp +decide [ Finset.filter_ne', Finset.filter_and, add_comm, add_left_comm ];
    congr 1 with x ; aesop;
  · grind

/-- **Incidence-count identity** (interior form): for a graph with at least one edge,
`degree v = 2 * interiorCount v + startIndicator v + endIndicator v`. -/
theorem degree_eq_interior (T : EulerTrail G) (hE : 1 ≤ G.nE) (v : Fin G.nV) :
    G.degree v = 2 * T.interiorCount v + T.startIndicator v + T.endIndicator v := by
  grind +suggestions

/-- **Parity consequence**: every vertex that is neither the start nor the end of an Eulerian
trail has even degree. -/
theorem degree_even_of_ne (T : EulerTrail G) (v : Fin G.nV)
    (h0 : v ≠ T.startVertex) (h1 : v ≠ T.endVertex) : Even (G.degree v) := by
  -- By definition of $T$, we know that $T.startIndicator v = 0$ and $T.endIndicator v = 0$.
  have h_start_end_zero : T.startIndicator v = 0 ∧ T.endIndicator v = 0 := by
    exact ⟨ if_neg h0.symm, if_neg h1.symm ⟩;
  exact even_iff_two_dvd.mpr ( by have := degree_add_indicators T v; aesop )

/-- **Main theorem**: in a finite multigraph admitting an Eulerian trail, the set of odd-degree
vertices has cardinality at most `2`. -/
theorem odd_degree_vertices_le_two (T : EulerTrail G) :
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun v => Odd (G.degree v))).card ≤ 2 := by
  -- By definition of $oddSet$, we know that every vertex in $oddSet$ has an odd degree.
  have h_oddSet_subset : Finset.filter (fun v => Odd (G.degree v)) (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin G.nV)) ⊆ {T.startVertex, T.endVertex} := by
    intro v hv; by_cases h0 : v = T.startVertex <;> by_cases h1 : v = T.endVertex <;> simp_all +decide ;
    exact hv.elim fun k hk => by have := degree_even_of_ne T v h0 h1; simp_all +decide [ parity_simps ] ;
  exact le_trans ( Finset.card_le_card h_oddSet_subset ) ( Finset.card_insert_le _ _ )

end EulerTrail

end Multigraph

end EulerianTrail

**Statement.** There exist genomes `C`, `D` connected by a "reachability" relation
(zig-zag of axiom changes) for which **no** single adjunction `C → D` exists, but a finite
composite of adjunctions *and* reflective localizations (categorical quotients) does.
Formally: the preorder generated by `IsMutation` is strictly coarser than the one generated by
`IsMutation` together with `CategoryTheory.Localization`.

**The key insight is** that `mutation_trans` already proves adjunctions compose, so the *only*
way the program's full "adjunctions **and** quotients" conjecture can be non-trivial is if
quotients are not themselves adjunctions on the nose — reflective localizations are adjunctions
but Gabriel–Zisman localizations in general are not.

**Why now?** We have an isolated, fully-proved `IsMutation` preorder; adding
`CategoryTheory.Localization` (already in Mathlib) lets us test the strictness directly,
without rebuilding any foundations.

**Statement.** A tropical-style mutation `(a ⋆ ·) ⊣ residual` on an ordered algebraic
structure is reversible (a genome equivalence) **iff** the operation `⋆` is cancellative
(group-like); it is strictly irreversible **iff** `⋆` is idempotent/absorbing.

group under `+`, while `tropClamp_irreversible` failed to be reversible precisely because `min`
is idempotent — the reversibility of a mutation is a *shadow of the invertibility of the
underlying operation*.

conjecture asks only to abstract the two proofs to an ordered-monoid hypothesis, which Mathlib's
`OrderedAddCommGroup` / `CanonicallyOrderedAddCommMonoid` hierarchy supports today.

**The key insight is** that equivalences of categories preserve all limits and colimits, so
*every* (co)limit-definable property is automatically invariant; the open and surprising half is

The Borsuk-Ulam theorem states that every continuous function f: S^n -> R^n maps some pair of antipodal points to the same value: f(x) = f(-x). Conjecture: Arrow's theorem is a corollary of Borsuk-Ulam. Specifically, define the 'preference sphere' S^{n-1} as the set of all preference profiles over n alternatives, where antipodal points represent opposite preferences (x prefers A > B > C, -x prefers C > B > A). import Mathlib
import Computation.BorsukUlamArrow

open Real

namespace BorsukUlamArrow

/-- The canonical "antipodal majority" social rule: a square wave whose value on
the profile `θ` is `+1` or `-1` according to the parity of `⌊θ/π⌋`. It models a
decisive rule that flips under preference reversal. -/
noncomputable def socialWave : ℝ → ℝ := fun θ => (-1 : ℝ) ^ (⌊θ / π⌋)

/-- `socialWave` is `2π`-periodic: it is a genuine function on the preference
circle. -/
theorem socialWave_periodic : Function.Periodic socialWave (2 * π) := by
  intro x
  unfold socialWave
  have hπ : π ≠ 0 := Real.pi_ne_zero
  have h1 : (x + 2 * π) / π = x / π + 2 := by field_simp
  rw [h1, Int.floor_add_ofNat, zpow_add₀ (by norm_num : (-1 : ℝ) ≠ 0)]
  norm_num

/-- `socialWave` flips under preference reversal `θ ↦ θ + π`. -/
theorem socialWave_reversal : ∀ θ, socialWave (θ + π) = - socialWave θ := by
  intro θ
  unfold socialWave
  have hπ : π ≠ 0 := Real.pi_ne_zero
  have h1 : (θ + π) / π = θ / π + 1 := by field_simp
  rw [h1, Int.floor_add_one, zpow_add₀ (by norm_num : (-1 : ℝ) ≠ 0)]
  ring

/-- `socialWave` is decisive: it never produces a tie. -/
theorem socialWave_decisive : ∀ θ, socialWave θ ≠ 0 := by
  intro θ; unfold socialWave; exact zpow_ne_zero _ (by norm_num)

/-- **Dropping continuity restores possibility.** A decisive,
reversal-respecting social welfare function *does* exist — so the impossibility
of the companion file is purely topological, not combinatorial. -/
theorem decisive_reversal_swf_exists :
    ∃ swf : ℝ → ℝ, (∀ θ, swf (θ + π) = - swf θ) ∧ (∀ θ, swf θ ≠ 0) :=
  ⟨socialWave, socialWave_reversal, socialWave_decisive⟩

/-- **The discontinuity of the antipodal majority is a theorem.** Because
`socialWave` is periodic, reversal-respecting and decisive, the impossibility
theorem `no_continuous_decisive_swf` forces it to be discontinuous — no ε–δ
argument required. This is the conjecture's "discontinuous or tied" alternative,
realized concretely. -/
theorem socialWave_not_continuous : ¬ Continuous socialWave := by
  intro hcont
  exact no_continuous_decisive_swf
    ⟨socialWave, ⟨hcont, socialWave_periodic⟩, socialWave_reversal, socialWave_decisive⟩

/-- **The topological Arrow dichotomy.** Every reversal-respecting social welfare
function is *either* not a continuous circle function (it must break topology)
*or* it is forced into a social tie somewhere. -/
theorem swf_dichotomy (swf : ℝ → ℝ) (hrev : ∀ θ, swf (θ + π) = - swf θ) :
    ¬ IsCircleFn swf ∨ ∃ θ, swf θ = 0 := by
  by_cases hc : IsCircleFn swf
  · right
    obtain ⟨θ, hθ⟩ := borsuk_ulam_one_dim hc
    rw [hrev θ] at hθ
    exact ⟨θ, by linarith⟩
  · left; exact hc

/-- The social tie set is antipode-stable: if profile `θ` is a tie, so is its
reversal `θ + π`. -/
theorem tie_set_antipodal {swf : ℝ → ℝ} (hrev : ∀ θ, swf (θ + π) = - swf θ)
    {θ : ℝ} (hθ : swf θ = 0) : swf (θ + π) = 0 := by
  rw [hrev θ, hθ, neg_zero]

end BorsukUlamArrow

import Mathlib

/-!
# A finite classical surrogate of integrated information for bit chains

This file develops a small, fully finished classical surrogate of the notion of
*integrated information* (`Φ`) restricted to finite probability distributions on
bit strings.  No quantum states, tensor networks, or measure theory appear: a
state of an `n`-bit chain is simply a probability mass function

```
p : (Fin n → Bool) → ℝ
```

with the usual nonnegativity and normalization hypotheses (`IsProbDist`).

## Cuts, recombination and marginals

For a *cut* `k ≤ n` we split a configuration into a left block `Fin k → Bool`
and a right block `Fin (n - k) → Bool`.  The combinatorial heart of the file is
the equivalence

```
cutEquiv k hk : (Fin k → Bool) × (Fin (n - k) → Bool) ≃ (Fin n → Bool)
```

built from `Fin.appendEquiv`, together with `recombine`, its forward map.  This
equivalence yields the Fubini-style sum decomposition
`sum_eq_sum_recombine`, the only nontrivial finite-sum manipulation needed.

The induced `leftMarginal` and `rightMarginal` are obtained by summing the
opposite block.

## Integrated-information surrogate

* `CutIndependent p hk` : `p` factorizes across the cut as the product of its two
  marginals.
* `FactorsAcross p hk`  : `p` factorizes as `pl a * pr b` for *some* left/right
  factors (a convenient sufficient condition).
* `cutScore p hk`       : `0` if the cut is independent, `1` otherwise.
* `PhiMin p`            : `0` if some nontrivial cut (`1 ≤ k < n`) is independent,
  `1` otherwise.  This is the surrogate "minimum information across all cuts":
  `Φ_min = 0` means the system decomposes into two non-interacting halves.

## Main results

* `cutIndependent_of_factorsAcross` : for a genuine probability distribution,
  any factorization through marginals-up-to-constant is a genuine cut
  independence.
* `cutScore_eq_zero_of_factorization` : a factorized distribution scores `0`.
* `phiMin_eq_zero_of_exists_factorization` : a nontrivial independent cut forces
  `PhiMin p = 0`.
* `productDist_isProbDist`, `productDist_cutIndependent` : the product of two
  probability distributions is a probability distribution that is independent at
  the defining cut.
* `uniform2_phiMin_zero` : the uniform distribution on a `2`-bit chain (built as a
  product across the middle cut) has `PhiMin = 0`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators
open scoped Classical

namespace ClassicalBitChain

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- A probability mass function on `n`-bit configurations: nonnegative and summing
to `1` over the finite configuration space `Fin n → Bool`. -/
structure IsProbDist (p : (Fin n → Bool) → ℝ) : Prop where
  nonneg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ p x
  sum_one : ∑ x, p x = 1

/-! ### Splitting and recombining configurations across a cut -/

/-- The combinatorial equivalence underlying a cut `k ≤ n`: a full configuration
is the same data as a pair of a left block and a right block. -/
noncomputable def cutEquiv (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) :
    (Fin k → Bool) × (Fin (n - k) → Bool) ≃ (Fin n → Bool) :=
  (Fin.appendEquiv k (n - k)).trans
    (Equiv.arrowCongr (finCongr (by omega : k + (n - k) = n)) (Equiv.refl Bool))

/-- Recombine a left block `a` and a right block `b` into a full configuration. -/
noncomputable def recombine (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n)
    (a : Fin k → Bool) (b : Fin (n - k) → Bool) : Fin n → Bool :=
  cutEquiv k hk (a, b)

/-- Inverse law: splitting a recombined configuration returns the original blocks. -/
@[simp] theorem cutEquiv_symm_recombine (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n)
    (a : Fin k → Bool) (b : Fin (n - k) → Bool) :
    (cutEquiv k hk).symm (recombine k hk a b) = (a, b) := by
  simp [recombine]

/-- Fubini decomposition of a finite sum over configurations along a cut. -/
theorem sum_eq_sum_recombine (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) (f : (Fin n → Bool) → ℝ) :
    ∑ x, f x = ∑ a, ∑ b, f (recombine k hk a b) := by
  rw [← Equiv.sum_comp (cutEquiv k hk) f, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
  rfl

/-! ### Marginals -/

/-- Left marginal of `p` at the cut `k`: sum over the right block. -/
noncomputable def leftMarginal (p : (Fin n → Bool) → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n)
    (a : Fin k → Bool) : ℝ :=
  ∑ b, p (recombine k hk a b)

/-- Right marginal of `p` at the cut `k`: sum over the left block. -/
noncomputable def rightMarginal (p : (Fin n → Bool) → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n)
    (b : Fin (n - k) → Bool) : ℝ :=
  ∑ a, p (recombine k hk a b)

/-! ### Cut independence and factorization -/

/-- `p` is independent across the cut `k` when it equals the product of its two
marginals there. -/
def CutIndependent (p : (Fin n → Bool) → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b, p (recombine k hk a b) = leftMarginal p k hk a * rightMarginal p k hk b

/-- `p` factorizes across the cut `k` when it is a product `pl a * pr b` for some
left/right factors. -/
def FactorsAcross (p : (Fin n → Bool) → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) : Prop :=
  ∃ (pl : (Fin k → Bool) → ℝ) (pr : (Fin (n - k) → Bool) → ℝ),
    ∀ a b, p (recombine k hk a b) = pl a * pr b

/-- For a genuine probability distribution, any factorization `p = pl ⬝ pr`
upgrades to genuine independence through the marginals. -/
theorem cutIndependent_of_factorsAcross {p : (Fin n → Bool) → ℝ} (hp : IsProbDist p)
    {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ n) (hf : FactorsAcross p k hk) :
    CutIndependent p k hk := by
  obtain ⟨pl, pr, hpl⟩ := hf
  -- the total mass factors as (∑ pl)(∑ pr) = 1
  have htot : (∑ a, pl a) * (∑ b, pr b) = 1 := by
    have h := hp.sum_one
    rw [sum_eq_sum_recombine k hk p] at h
    simp only [hpl] at h
    rw [Finset.sum_mul_sum]
    exact h
  intro a b
  have hL : leftMarginal p k hk a = pl a * (∑ b, pr b) := by
    simp only [leftMarginal, hpl, ← Finset.mul_sum]
  have hR : rightMarginal p k hk b = (∑ a, pl a) * pr b := by
    simp only [rightMarginal, hpl, ← Finset.sum_mul]
  rw [hL, hR, hpl]
  linear_combination (-(pl a * pr b)) * htot

/-! ### The cut score and the integrated-information surrogate `Φ_min` -/

/-- The bipartition score of the cut `k`: `0` if `p` is independent there, `1`
otherwise. -/
noncomputable def cutScore (p : (Fin n → Bool) → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) : ℕ :=
  if CutIndependent p k hk then 0 else 1

/-- A nontrivial cut splits the chain into two nonempty halves. -/
def NontrivialCut (n k : ℕ) : Prop := 1 ≤ k ∧ k < n

/-- The integrated-information surrogate: `0` if some nontrivial cut is independent,
`1` otherwise. -/
noncomputable def PhiMin (p : (Fin n → Bool) → ℝ) : ℕ :=
  if ∃ (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n), NontrivialCut n k ∧ CutIndependent p k hk then 0 else 1

/-- An independent cut scores `0`. -/
theorem cutScore_eq_zero_of_cutIndependent {p : (Fin n → Bool) → ℝ} {k : ℕ}
    (hk : k ≤ n) (h : CutIndependent p k hk) : cutScore p k hk = 0 := by
  simp [cutScore, h]

/-- An explicitly factorized probability distribution scores `0` at the cut. -/
theorem cutScore_eq_zero_of_factorization {p : (Fin n → Bool) → ℝ}
    (hp : IsProbDist p) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ n) (hf : FactorsAcross p k hk) :
    cutScore p k hk = 0 :=
  cutScore_eq_zero_of_cutIndependent hk (cutIndependent_of_factorsAcross hp hk hf)

/-- If some nontrivial cut is independent, the surrogate `Φ_min` vanishes. -/
theorem phiMin_eq_zero_of_exists_cutIndependent {p : (Fin n → Bool) → ℝ}
    (h : ∃ (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n), NontrivialCut n k ∧ CutIndependent p k hk) :
    PhiMin p = 0 := by
  unfold PhiMin
  rw [if_pos h]

/-- If some nontrivial cut factorizes the probability distribution, `Φ_min = 0`. -/
theorem phiMin_eq_zero_of_exists_factorization {p : (Fin n → Bool) → ℝ}
    (hp : IsProbDist p)
    (h : ∃ (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n), NontrivialCut n k ∧ FactorsAcross p k hk) :
    PhiMin p = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨k, hk, hnt, hf⟩ := h
  exact phiMin_eq_zero_of_exists_cutIndependent
    ⟨k, hk, hnt, cutIndependent_of_factorsAcross hp hk hf⟩

/-! ### Product distributions -/

/-- The product distribution built from a left factor `pl` and a right factor `pr`
across the cut `k`. -/
noncomputable def productDist {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ n)
    (pl : (Fin k → Bool) → ℝ) (pr : (Fin (n - k) → Bool) → ℝ) :
    (Fin n → Bool) → ℝ :=
  fun x => pl ((cutEquiv k hk).symm x).1 * pr ((cutEquiv k hk).symm x).2

@[simp] theorem productDist_recombine {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ n)
    (pl : (Fin k → Bool) → ℝ) (pr : (Fin (n - k) → Bool) → ℝ)
    (a : Fin k → Bool) (b : Fin (n - k) → Bool) :
    productDist hk pl pr (recombine k hk a b) = pl a * pr b := by
  simp [productDist]

/-- The product distribution factorizes across its defining cut. -/
theorem productDist_factorsAcross {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ n)
    (pl : (Fin k → Bool) → ℝ) (pr : (Fin (n - k) → Bool) → ℝ) :
    FactorsAcross (productDist hk pl pr) k hk :=
  ⟨pl, pr, fun a b => productDist_recombine hk pl pr a b⟩

/-- The product of two probability distributions is a probability distribution. -/
theorem productDist_isProbDist {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ n)
    {pl : (Fin k → Bool) → ℝ} {pr : (Fin (n - k) → Bool) → ℝ}
    (hpl0 : ∀ a, 0 ≤ pl a) (hpr0 : ∀ b, 0 ≤ pr b)
    (hpl1 : ∑ a, pl a = 1) (hpr1 : ∑ b, pr b = 1) :
    IsProbDist (productDist hk pl pr) where
  nonneg x := by
    have := cutEquiv k hk |>.symm x
    exact mul_nonneg (hpl0 _) (hpr0 _)
  sum_one := by
    rw [sum_eq_sum_recombine k hk]
    simp only [productDist_recombine]
    rw [← Finset.sum_mul_sum, hpl1, hpr1, one_mul]

/-- The product of two probability distributions is cut-independent at its
defining cut. -/
theorem productDist_cutIndependent {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ n)
    {pl : (Fin k → Bool) → ℝ} {pr : (Fin (n - k) → Bool) → ℝ}
    (hpl0 : ∀ a, 0 ≤ pl a) (hpr0 : ∀ b, 0 ≤ pr b)
    (hpl1 : ∑ a, pl a = 1) (hpr1 : ∑ b, pr b = 1) :
    CutIndependent (productDist hk pl pr) k hk :=
  cutIndependent_of_factorsAcross
    (productDist_isProbDist hk hpl0 hpr0 hpl1 hpr1) hk
    (productDist_factorsAcross hk pl pr)

/-! ### A concrete example: the uniform `2`-bit chain -/

/-- The uniform distribution on a `2`-bit chain, realized as the product of two
fair single-bit distributions across the middle cut `k = 1`. -/
noncomputable def uniform2 : (Fin 2 → Bool) → ℝ :=
  productDist (n := 2) (k := 1) (by norm_num) (fun _ => 1 / 2) (fun _ => 1 / 2)

theorem uniform2_isProbDist : IsProbDist uniform2 := by
  apply productDist_isProbDist
  · intro a; norm_num
  · intro b; norm_num
  · simp [Finset.sum_const]
  · simp [Finset.sum_const]

/-- The uniform `2`-bit chain has vanishing integrated-information surrogate: it
splits as two independent fair bits across the middle cut. -/
theorem uniform2_phiMin_zero : PhiMin uniform2 = 0 := by
  apply phiMin_eq_zero_of_exists_factorization uniform2_isProbDist
  refine ⟨1, by norm_num, ⟨le_refl 1, by norm_num⟩, ?_⟩
  exact productDist_factorsAcross (n := 2) (k := 1) (by norm_num) _ _

end ClassicalBitChain

/-!
# Entropy-Complexity Bridge: From Compression to Information Bounds

This file establishes formal bridges between algorithmic compression/complexity
and entropy-like information bounds on finite types. The central theme is:

> **Compression controls entropy-like support complexity.**
> If a finite family of objects can be injectively encoded into a bounded
> code space, then the family's cardinality (and hence its log-cardinality,
> a uniform entropy surrogate) is bounded by the code space size.

## Main Results

### Finite cardinality bounds from injective encodings
- `card_le_of_injective_to_fin`: Injective map to `Fin N` bounds cardinality by `N`.
- `card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code`: Injective map to `Fin (2^k)` bounds cardinality by `2^k`.
- `card_le_two_pow_of_injective_bitcode`: Injective map to `Fin k → Bool` bounds cardinality by `2^k`.
- `card_range_le_two_pow_of_bitlength_bound`: Range of a map to `Fin (2^k)` has size ≤ `2^k`.

### Entropy bounds
- `EntropyBound`: Predicate `Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k`, the finite uniform entropy inequality.
- `entropyBound_of_injective_code`: Injective code implies entropy bound.
- `uniform_entropy_le_code_length`: Log-cardinality bounded by code length.

### Support monotonicity (data processing)
- `support_entropy_monotone_under_map`: `|range f| ≤ |α|`.
- `card_range_le_card_codomain`: `|range f| ≤ |β|`.
- `support_entropy_comp_monotone`: `|range (g ∘ f)| ≤ |range f|` — deterministic data processing.

### Cross-domain bridge
- `complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound`: Connects compressor bounds
  to finite cardinality control.

## Mathematical Significance

These theorems form the combinatorial skeleton of the source coding principle
and create a formal route from Kolmogorov-style complexity bounds to
entropy/information inequalities. The composition monotonicity theorem
`support_entropy_comp_monotone` is a combinatorial shadow of the
**data processing inequality**: deterministic post-processing cannot
increase the number of distinguishable outputs.
-/

open Set Function Finset Fintype

/-! ## Section 1: Core Finite Cardinality Bounds -/

/-- An injective map from a finite type to `Fin N` implies the source has
at most `N` elements. This is the fundamental counting principle underlying
all compression-to-entropy arguments. -/
theorem card_le_of_injective_to_fin
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {N : ℕ}
    (f : α → Fin N) (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ N := by
  calc Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card (Fin N) := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hf
    _ = N := Fintype.card_fin N

/-- An injective encoding into `Fin (2^k)` bounds source cardinality by `2^k`.
This is the exponential form of the entropy bound: if objects can be
described by `k`-bit codes, there are at most `2^k` of them. -/
theorem card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k :=
  card_le_of_injective_to_fin enc henc

/-- The cardinality of the function space `Fin k → Bool` is exactly `2^k`.
This witnesses bitstrings of length `k` as a code space of size `2^k`. -/
theorem fintype_card_fun_bool (k : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card (Fin k → Bool) = 2^k := by
  simp [Fintype.card_fin, Fintype.card_bool]

/-- An injective encoding into explicit bitstrings `Fin k → Bool` bounds
cardinality by `2^k`. This is the most concrete form: each element gets
a unique `k`-bit string, so there can be at most `2^k` elements. -/
theorem card_le_two_pow_of_injective_bitcode
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (f : α → (Fin k → Bool)) (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k := by
  calc Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card (Fin k → Bool) := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hf
    _ = 2^k := fintype_card_fun_bool k

/-- The range of any map into `Fin (2^k)` has at most `2^k` elements.
This does not require injectivity — it bounds the number of distinguishable
outputs of any encoding scheme. -/
theorem card_range_le_two_pow_of_bitlength_bound
    {n k : ℕ} (f : Fin n → Fin (2^k)) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ 2^k := by
  calc Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card (Fin (2^k)) := Fintype.card_subtype_le _
    _ = 2^k := Fintype.card_fin _

/-! ## Section 2: Entropy Bound Predicate and Logarithmic Form -/

/-- `EntropyBound α k` asserts that the uniform entropy of the finite type `α`
is at most `k` bits: equivalently, `|α| ≤ 2^k`. This is the finite
combinatorial skeleton of the source coding bound `H(X) ≤ k` for a
uniform source over `α` encoded with `k`-bit codewords. -/
def EntropyBound (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k

/-- An injective encoding into `k`-bit codes implies the entropy bound.
This is the formal finite-uniform entropy inequality: if every element
of `α` receives a unique `k`-bit code, then `H(α) ≤ k`. -/
theorem entropyBound_of_injective_code
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    EntropyBound α k :=
  card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code enc henc

/-
Logarithmic form of the entropy bound: if `α` injects into `Fin (2^k)`,
then `log₂ |α| ≤ k`. Uses `Nat.log` which is the floor of the logarithm.
-/
theorem uniform_entropy_le_code_length
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Nat.log 2 (Fintype.card α) ≤ k := by
  -- We have card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code which gives Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k.
  -- Taking the base-2 logarithm is monotonic, so log₂ |α| ≤ log₂ 2^k = k.
  have hcard : Fintype.card α ≤ 2 ^ k := by
    apply card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code enc henc
  exact (Nat.log_mono_right hcard).trans (Nat.log_pow (by norm_num : 1 < 2) k).le

/-- For any injective encoding `α → Fin (2^k)`, the
log-cardinality of `α` is bounded by `k`. -/
theorem log_card_range_le_of_embedding_into_bitstrings
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Nat.log 2 (Fintype.card α) ≤ k :=
  uniform_entropy_le_code_length enc henc

/-! ## Section 3: Support Monotonicity — Data Processing -/

/-- The range of a map has at most as many elements as its domain.
This is a combinatorial form of the principle that deterministic
processing cannot create new distinguishable outputs. -/
theorem support_entropy_monotone_under_map
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq β]
    (f : α → β) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card α :=
  Fintype.card_range_le f

/-- The range of a map has at most as many elements as the codomain.
This is the trivial but useful fact that range ⊆ codomain implies
the cardinality inequality. -/
theorem card_range_le_card_codomain
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    (f : α → β) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card β :=
  Fintype.card_subtype_le _

/-
**Combinatorial Data Processing Inequality.**
Composition cannot increase the number of distinguishable outputs:
`|range (g ∘ f)| ≤ |range f|`. This is the finite combinatorial
shadow of the data processing inequality `H(g(X)) ≤ H(X)` for
deterministic channels.
-/
theorem support_entropy_comp_monotone
    {α β γ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
    (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range (g ∘ f)) ≤ Fintype.card (Set.range f) := by
  -- By definition of range, we know that every element in the range of `g ∘ f` is of the form `g (f a)` for some `a ∈ α`.
  have h_range : Set.range (g ∘ f) = g '' Set.range f := by
    grind +splitIndPred;
  simp +decide only [h_range, card_ofFinset];
  refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_image_le ) _;
  exact Finset.card_le_card fun x hx => by aesop;

/-! ## Section 4: Compression Lower Bounds -/

/-
If a type has more than `2^k` elements, no injective encoding into
`k`-bit codes exists. This is the compression impossibility theorem:
you cannot losslessly compress a family of size `> 2^k` into `k` bits.
-/
theorem no_injective_code_of_card_gt
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (hcard : 2^k < Fintype.card α) :
    ¬ ∃ f : α → Fin (2^k), Function.Injective f := by
  exact fun ⟨ f, hf ⟩ => not_le_of_gt hcard ( card_le_of_injective_to_fin f hf )

/-! ## Section 5: Subadditivity Under Products -/

/-
Product encoding: if `α` has at most `2^k` elements and `β` has at most
`2^ℓ` elements, then `α × β` has at most `2^(k + ℓ)` elements.
This is entropy subadditivity: `H(X, Y) ≤ H(X) + H(Y)`.
-/
theorem entropyBound_prod_of_entropyBound
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] {k ℓ : ℕ}
    (hα : EntropyBound α k) (hβ : EntropyBound β ℓ) :
    EntropyBound (α × β) (k + ℓ) := by
  unfold EntropyBound at *;
  simpa only [ pow_add, Fintype.card_prod ] using Nat.mul_le_mul hα hβ

/-! ## Section 6: Cross-Domain Bridge to Compression-Complexity -/

namespace EntropyComplexityBridge

/-- An invertible compressor with idempotence, length-bounding, and inverse. -/
structure InvertibleCompressor where
  compress : List Bool → List Bool
  decompress : List Bool → List Bool
  hidem : ∀ s, compress (compress s) = compress s
  hlen : ∀ s, (compress s).length ≤ s.length
  hstrict : ∀ s, compress s ≠ s → (compress s).length < s.length
  hinv : ∀ s, decompress (compress s) = s

/-
**Complexity bound implies finite entropy bound (bridge theorem).**

Given an invertible compressor `C` and a finite family of binary strings,
if every element has compressed length ≤ `k`, then the family has at most
`2^(k+1)` elements (since there are `2^(k+1) - 1` binary strings of
length ≤ `k`).

This is the key bridge: algorithmic complexity upper bounds (via compressors)
imply entropy upper bounds (via cardinality control).
-/
theorem complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound
    (C : InvertibleCompressor)
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (embed : α → List Bool)
    (hembed : Function.Injective embed)
    {k : ℕ}
    (hbound : ∀ a : α, (C.compress (embed a)).length ≤ k) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^(k+1) := by
  -- We know that `compress` is injective and its image is contained in the set of lists of length ≤ k.
  have h_image : Finset.card (Finset.image (fun a => C.compress (embed a)) Finset.univ) ≤ 2^(k+1) - 1 := by
    -- The set of lists of length ≤ k is finite and has cardinality 2^(k+1) - 1.
    have h_card : Finset.card (Finset.filter (fun l => l.length ≤ k) (Finset.biUnion (Finset.range (k + 1)) (fun i => Finset.image (fun l : Fin i → Bool => List.ofFn l) (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin i → Bool)))) ) ≤ 2^(k+1) - 1 := by
      refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_filter_le _ _ ) _;
      refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_biUnion_le ) _;
      rw [ Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i hi => Finset.card_image_of_injective _ fun x y hxy => by simpa [ funext_iff ] using hxy ] ; simp +decide [ Nat.geomSum_eq ];
    refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_le_card _ ) h_card;
    simp +decide [ Finset.subset_iff ];
    exact fun a => ⟨ ⟨ _, hbound a, fun i => ( C.compress ( embed a ) |> List.get <| ⟨ i, by linarith [ hbound a, i.2 ] ⟩ ), by simp +decide ⟩, hbound a ⟩;
  rw [ Finset.card_image_of_injective _ fun a b hab => hembed <| by have := C.hinv ( embed a ) ; have := C.hinv ( embed b ) ; aesop ] at h_image ; exact le_trans h_image ( Nat.sub_le _ _ )

/-- **Finite family complexity certificate.**
If a compressor certifies that every element of a finite type has
compressed representation of length ≤ `k`, this yields an entropy
bound on the type. -/
theorem entropyBound_of_compressor
    (C : InvertibleCompressor)
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (embed : α → List Bool)
    (hembed : Function.Injective embed)
    {k : ℕ}
    (hbound : ∀ a : α, (C.compress (embed a)).length ≤ k) :
    EntropyBound α (k + 1) :=
  complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound C embed hembed hbound

end EntropyComplexityBridge

import Mathlib

/-! # A complete formal core for the tropical Fermat equation over `ℤ`

This file develops a small, fully verified core of *tropical* (min-plus) algebra over
the integers and uses it to classify solutions of the binary tropical Fermat equation.

## The min-plus convention

We work in the **min-plus** semiring structure on `ℤ`:

* tropical addition is the minimum, `tadd a b = min a b`;
* tropical multiplication is the ordinary integer addition, `tmul a b = a + b`;
* tropical exponentiation (repeated tropical multiplication) is multiplication by the
  exponent, `tpow a n = (n : ℤ) * a`.

## The binary tropical Fermat equation and the `n = 0` / `0 < n` split

The binary tropical Fermat equation is

`TropFermatEq n x y z : min ((n:ℤ)*x) ((n:ℤ)*y) = (n:ℤ)*z`.

The classification genuinely depends on whether the exponent vanishes:

* when `n = 0`, all three tropical powers collapse to `0`, so the equation holds for
  *every* `x, y, z` (`tropFermat_zero`);
* when `0 < n`, multiplication by the strictly positive integer `(n : ℤ)` both preserves
  and reflects order, so the equation is equivalent to `z = min x y`
  (`tropFermat_pos_iff`) and to the order-theoretic form
  `z ≤ x ∧ z ≤ y ∧ (z = x ∨ z = y)` (`tropFermat_pos_iff_order`).

We are careful **not** to claim exponent-independence without the `0 < n` hypothesis.

## One-variable tropical polynomials

We represent a one-variable tropical polynomial as a `List (ℤ × ℤ)` of affine terms
`(slope, intercept)`, evaluated affinely by `affEval` and tropically by `tropEval`
(the pointwise minimum of the affine terms). We prove the basic normal-form facts:
each term is an upper bound, the value is attained on the support, the value is the least
of the affine values (`tropEval_isLeast`), and monotonicity under nonnegative slopes.

Finally `tropFermat_as_poly` identifies the function `x ↦ min ((n:ℤ)*x) ((n:ℤ)*y)`
governing the Fermat equation as a concrete tropical polynomial evaluation.
-/

namespace Tropical.FermatCore

/-! ## Tropical operations on `ℤ` (min-plus convention) -/

/-- Tropical addition: the minimum. -/
def tadd (a b : ℤ) : ℤ := min a b

/-- Tropical multiplication: ordinary integer addition. -/
def tmul (a b : ℤ) : ℤ := a + b

/-- Tropical exponentiation: multiplication by the (natural-number) exponent. -/
def tpow (a : ℤ) (n : ℕ) : ℤ := (n : ℤ) * a

@[simp] theorem tadd_def (a b : ℤ) : tadd a b = min a b := rfl
@[simp] theorem tmul_def (a b : ℤ) : tmul a b = a + b := rfl
@[simp] theorem tpow_def (a : ℤ) (n : ℕ) : tpow a n = (n : ℤ) * a := rfl

/-- Tropical addition is commutative. -/
theorem tadd_comm (a b : ℤ) : tadd a b = tadd b a := by
  simp [tadd, min_comm]

/-- Tropical addition is associative. -/
theorem tadd_assoc (a b c : ℤ) : tadd (tadd a b) c = tadd a (tadd b c) := by
  simp [tadd, min_assoc]

/-- Tropical multiplication is commutative. -/
theorem tmul_comm (a b : ℤ) : tmul a b = tmul b a := by
  simp [tmul, add_comm]

/-- Tropical multiplication is associative. -/
theorem tmul_assoc (a b c : ℤ) : tmul (tmul a b) c = tmul a (tmul b c) := by
  simp [tmul, add_assoc]

/-- Distributivity of tropical multiplication over tropical addition. -/
theorem tmul_tadd (a b c : ℤ) : tmul a (tadd b c) = tadd (tmul a b) (tmul a c) := by
  simp only [tmul, tadd]; omega

/-- Right distributivity of tropical multiplication over tropical addition. -/
theorem tadd_tmul (a b c : ℤ) : tmul (tadd a b) c = tadd (tmul a c) (tmul b c) := by
  simp only [tmul, tadd]; omega

/-! ## Order characterization of `min` -/

/-- The reusable characterization of `min`: `z` is the minimum of `x` and `y` exactly when
it is a lower bound that is attained. -/
theorem eq_min_iff (x y z : ℤ) :
    z = min x y ↔ z ≤ x ∧ z ≤ y ∧ (z = x ∨ z = y) := by
  omega

/-- `tadd` form of `eq_min_iff`. -/
theorem eq_tadd_iff (x y z : ℤ) :
    z = tadd x y ↔ z ≤ x ∧ z ≤ y ∧ (z = x ∨ z = y) := by
  simp only [tadd]; omega

/-! ## The binary tropical Fermat equation -/

/-- The binary tropical Fermat equation in the min-plus convention:
`min ((n:ℤ)*x) ((n:ℤ)*y) = (n:ℤ)*z`. -/
def TropFermatEq (n : ℕ) (x y z : ℤ) : Prop :=
  tadd (tpow x n) (tpow y n) = tpow z n

theorem tropFermatEq_def (n : ℕ) (x y z : ℤ) :
    TropFermatEq n x y z ↔ min ((n : ℤ) * x) ((n : ℤ) * y) = (n : ℤ) * z := by
  simp [TropFermatEq, tadd, tpow]

/-- For exponent `0`, the tropical Fermat equation holds for all `x, y, z`. -/
theorem tropFermat_zero (x y z : ℤ) : TropFermatEq 0 x y z := by
  simp [TropFermatEq, tadd, tpow]

/-- For positive exponent `n`, the tropical Fermat equation is equivalent to `z = min x y`.
This crucially uses `0 < n`: multiplication by the strictly positive integer `(n : ℤ)`
both preserves and reflects order. -/
theorem tropFermat_pos_iff {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x y z : ℤ) :
    TropFermatEq n x y z ↔ z = min x y := by
  rw [tropFermatEq_def]
  have h0 : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (n : ℤ) := by positivity
  have hne : (n : ℤ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hn.ne'
  rw [← mul_min_of_nonneg x y h0]
  constructor
  · intro h; exact (mul_left_cancel₀ hne h).symm
  · intro h; rw [h]

/-- The order-theoretic form of the classification for positive exponent. -/
theorem tropFermat_pos_iff_order {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x y z : ℤ) :
    TropFermatEq n x y z ↔ z ≤ x ∧ z ≤ y ∧ (z = x ∨ z = y) := by
  rw [tropFermat_pos_iff hn, eq_min_iff]

/-! ## One-variable tropical polynomials -/

/-- Affine evaluation of a term `(slope, intercept)` at a point `x`. -/
def affEval (t : ℤ × ℤ) (x : ℤ) : ℤ := t.1 * x + t.2

@[simp] theorem affEval_def (t : ℤ × ℤ) (x : ℤ) : affEval t x = t.1 * x + t.2 := rfl

/-- Tropical (min-plus) evaluation of a one-variable tropical polynomial, represented as a
list of affine terms. It is the pointwise minimum of the affine evaluations of the terms.
The empty list is given the dummy value `0`; all interesting lemmas assume nonemptiness. -/
def tropEval : List (ℤ × ℤ) → ℤ → ℤ
  | [], _ => 0
  | [t], x => affEval t x
  | t :: ts, x => min (affEval t x) (tropEval ts x)

@[simp] theorem tropEval_nil (x : ℤ) : tropEval [] x = 0 := rfl

theorem tropEval_singleton (t : ℤ × ℤ) (x : ℤ) : tropEval [t] x = affEval t x := rfl

theorem tropEval_cons (t s : ℤ × ℤ) (ts : List (ℤ × ℤ)) (x : ℤ) :
    tropEval (t :: s :: ts) x = min (affEval t x) (tropEval (s :: ts) x) := rfl

/-- Tropical evaluation is bounded above by each listed affine term. -/
theorem tropEval_le_of_mem {p : List (ℤ × ℤ)} {t : ℤ × ℤ} {x : ℤ}
    (ht : t ∈ p) : tropEval p x ≤ affEval t x := by
  induction' p with p hp;
  · contradiction;
  · cases hp <;> simp_all +decide [ tropEval ];
    grind +splitIndPred

/-- On a nonempty support, tropical evaluation equals the affine value of some term. -/
theorem tropEval_mem {p : List (ℤ × ℤ)} (x : ℤ) (hp : p ≠ []) :
    ∃ t ∈ p, tropEval p x = affEval t x := by
  induction' p with t p ih;
  · contradiction;
  · cases p <;> simp_all +decide [ tropEval ];
    grind

/-- Tropical evaluation is exactly the least of the affine values of the terms: it is the
pointwise minimum of finitely many affine-linear functions. -/
theorem tropEval_isLeast {p : List (ℤ × ℤ)} (x : ℤ) (hp : p ≠ []) :
    IsLeast {v : ℤ | ∃ t ∈ p, v = affEval t x} (tropEval p x) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨t, ht, he⟩ := tropEval_mem x hp
    exact ⟨t, ht, he⟩
  · rintro v ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩
    exact tropEval_le_of_mem ht

/-- Monotonicity of tropical evaluation when all slopes are nonnegative. -/
theorem tropEval_mono {p : List (ℤ × ℤ)} (hp : ∀ t ∈ p, 0 ≤ t.1)
    {x x' : ℤ} (hx : x ≤ x') : tropEval p x ≤ tropEval p x' := by
  induction' p with t p ih;
  · rfl;
  · cases p <;> simp_all +decide [ tropEval ];
    · exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hx hp;
    · exact Or.inl ( mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hx hp.1 )

/-! ## Connecting the Fermat classification to the polynomial viewpoint -/

/-- The function `x ↦ min ((n:ℤ)*x) ((n:ℤ)*y)` governing the binary Fermat equation is the
evaluation of the concrete two-term tropical polynomial `[(n, 0), (0, n*y)]`. -/
theorem tropFermat_as_poly (n : ℕ) (x y : ℤ) :
    tropEval [((n : ℤ), 0), (0, (n : ℤ) * y)] x = tadd (tpow x n) (tpow y n) := by
  simp only [tropEval, affEval, tadd, tpow, zero_add, add_zero, zero_mul]

/-- Restatement of the positive-exponent classification through the polynomial evaluation:
the Fermat equation holds iff the tropical polynomial value equals `(n:ℤ)*z`. -/
theorem tropFermat_poly_iff {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x y z : ℤ) :
    tropEval [((n : ℤ), 0), (0, (n : ℤ) * y)] x = tpow z n ↔ z = min x y := by
  rw [tropFermat_as_poly]
  exact tropFermat_pos_iff hn x y z

end Tropical.FermatCore

This research cycle established the core dichotomy: the classical Fermat equation
`aⁿ + bⁿ = cⁿ` has no nontrivial solutions for `n ≥ 3`, while its tropical analogue
`max(n•a, n•b) = n•c` is **always** uniquely solvable (by `c = max a b`). The engine is the
monotonicity of `x ↦ n•x`, which makes it commute with `max`/`min`. We formalized the
max-plus and min-plus identities, existence, uniqueness, classification, a multivariable
(`Finset.sup'`) generalization, the tropical Fermat curve, and a faithful embedding into
Mathlib's genuine `Tropical ℝ` semiring (all in `Core.lean`, 0 sorries).

Below are bold, precise, testable conjectures for follow-up cycles.

## C1. Tropical Fermat over arbitrary scalar exponents (semimodules)
**Conjecture.** Replace the natural-number exponent `n` by a scalar `r` from an ordered
semiring acting on an ordered module `M`. Then for `r > 0`, `max (r • a) (r • b) = r • max a b`
holds and the solution `c = max a b` is unique; for `r = 0` it degenerates (every `c` works);
for `r < 0` (when defined) the identity flips to `min`. 
*Test:* formalize `r : ℝ≥0` acting on `ℝ` via `smul`, prove the trichotomy, and identify the
exact `OrderedSMul`/`PosSMulStrictMono` hypotheses that make uniqueness hold.

**Conjecture.** For every `n ≥ 1` and every number of variables `k ≥ 2`, the tropical
Fermat hypersurface `corner-locus of  max_i (n•xᵢ) ⊕ 0` is a nonempty, pure-dimensional,
balanced polyhedral complex whose vertex is the origin, with exactly `k+1` top-dimensional
rays/cells through it. We proved the `k = 2` skeleton (symmetry, origin vertex, diagonal
ray). *Test:* generalize `OnFermatCurve` to `k` variables via `Finset`, prove nonemptiness
and the "attained at least twice somewhere" balancing condition for all `k`.

**Conjecture.** Define an `ε`-approximate tropical Fermat solution by
`|max (n•a) (n•b) − n•c| ≤ ε`. Then `c` is forced into the interval
`[max a b − ε/n, max a b + ε/n]`; in particular as `n → ∞` the approximate solution set
collapses to the exact one at rate `Θ(1/n)`. *Test:* prove the two-sided bound and the
collapse rate; connect to the `TropicalEquivalenceInvariance` gap-stability results already
in the catalog.

import Mathlib

/-! # Eulerian Trail Parity

A minimal, self-contained finite-multigraph development of the parity
theorem underlying Euler's theorem on Eulerian trails:

* a finite multigraph `Multigraph nV nE` stores an ordered endpoint pair for
  each edge (`ends : Fin nE → Fin nV × Fin nV`); loops and parallel edges are
  allowed;
* `degree G v` is the sum over all edges of the two endpoint indicators, so a
  loop at `v` contributes `2`;
* an `EulerianTrail G` is a walk that uses every edge exactly once (encoded by a
  bijection `edgeAt` on edge indices), with a compatibility condition saying the
  `i`-th traversed edge joins the `i`-th and `(i+1)`-th vertices of the walk in
  either orientation.

The main results are:

* `degree_visit_identity` — a degree/visit-count identity with endpoint
  correction;
* `even_degree_of_internal` — every vertex other than the two trail endpoints
  has even degree;
* `odd_degree_mem_endpoints` — an odd-degree vertex is the start or the end;
* `odd_degree_vertices_le_two` — at most two vertices have odd degree.
-/

namespace EulerianTrailParity

open scoped BigOperators

/-- A finite multigraph on vertex set `Fin nV` with `nE` edges, each edge given
by an ordered pair of endpoints.  Loops (`(v, v)`) and parallel edges are
allowed. -/
structure Multigraph (nV nE : ℕ) where
  ends : Fin nE → Fin nV × Fin nV

variable {nV nE : ℕ}

/-- The degree of a vertex: the number of edge-endpoints landing on it.  A loop
at `v` contributes `2`. -/
def degree (G : Multigraph nV nE) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  ∑ e : Fin nE,
    ((if (G.ends e).1 = v then 1 else 0) + (if (G.ends e).2 = v then 1 else 0))

/-- An Eulerian trail of `G`: a walk through `nE + 1` vertices together with a
bijection `edgeAt` selecting, for each step, the edge traversed at that step;
each traversed edge joins consecutive walk vertices in some orientation. -/
structure EulerianTrail (G : Multigraph nV nE) where
  walk : Fin (nE + 1) → Fin nV
  edgeAt : Fin nE → Fin nE
  edge_perm : Function.Bijective edgeAt
  compat : ∀ i : Fin nE,
      ((G.ends (edgeAt i)).1 = walk i.castSucc ∧ (G.ends (edgeAt i)).2 = walk i.succ) ∨
      ((G.ends (edgeAt i)).1 = walk i.succ ∧ (G.ends (edgeAt i)).2 = walk i.castSucc)

variable {G : Multigraph nV nE}

/-- The indicator of a vertex appearing at a given walk position. -/
def visit (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) (j : Fin (nE + 1)) : ℕ :=
  if T.walk j = v then 1 else 0

/-
Finite-sum helper: a sum over `Fin (n+1)` splits as the `castSucc` part plus
the last term.
-/
lemma sum_castSucc_eq (n : ℕ) (f : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ) :
    (∑ i : Fin n, f i.castSucc) + f (Fin.last n) = ∑ j : Fin (n + 1), f j := by
  rw [ Fin.sum_univ_castSucc ]

/-
Finite-sum helper: a sum over `Fin (n+1)` splits as the head term plus the
`succ` part.
-/
lemma sum_succ_eq (n : ℕ) (f : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ) :
    f 0 + (∑ i : Fin n, f i.succ) = ∑ j : Fin (n + 1), f j := by
  rw [ Fin.sum_univ_succ ]

/-
The degree, computed along the trail: reindexing the degree sum by the edge
bijection and using the compatibility condition, the degree of `v` equals the
number of consecutive walk-position pairs landing on `v`.
-/
lemma degree_eq_sum (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) :
    degree G v =
      ∑ i : Fin nE, (visit T v i.castSucc + visit T v i.succ) := by
  -- By definition of `degree`, we know that
  unfold degree;
  rw [ ← Equiv.sum_comp ( Equiv.ofBijective ( T.edgeAt ) T.edge_perm ) ];
  congr with i;
  cases T.compat i <;> simp +decide [ *, visit ];
  ring

/-
Degree/visit-count identity with endpoint correction:
`degree G v` plus the start- and end-indicators equals twice the total number of
walk positions visiting `v`.
-/
lemma degree_visit_identity (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) :
    degree G v + visit T v 0 + visit T v (Fin.last nE)
      = 2 * ∑ j : Fin (nE + 1), visit T v j := by
  rw [ degree_eq_sum T v, Finset.sum_add_distrib ];
  linarith! [ sum_castSucc_eq nE ( fun i => visit T v i ), sum_succ_eq nE ( fun i => visit T v i ) ]

/-
Every vertex that is neither the start nor the end of the trail has even
degree.
-/
lemma even_degree_of_internal (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV)
    (h0 : T.walk 0 ≠ v) (hlast : T.walk (Fin.last nE) ≠ v) :
    Even (degree G v) := by
  -- By `h0` and `hlast`, `visit T v 0 = 0` and `visit T v (Fin.last nE) = 0`.
  have hv0 : visit T v 0 = 0 := by
    exact if_neg h0
  have hvlast : visit T v (Fin.last nE) = 0 := by
    exact if_neg hlast;
  exact even_iff_two_dvd.mpr ⟨ ∑ j : Fin ( nE + 1 ), visit T v j, by linarith [ degree_visit_identity T v ] ⟩

/-
If a vertex has odd degree, it is the start or the end of the trail.
-/
lemma odd_degree_mem_endpoints (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV)
    (hodd : Odd (degree G v)) :
    v = T.walk 0 ∨ v = T.walk (Fin.last nE) := by
  grind +suggestions

/-
The set of odd-degree vertices is contained in the two-element set of trail
endpoints.
-/
lemma oddVerts_subset (T : EulerianTrail G) :
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun v => Odd (degree G v))) ⊆
      {T.walk 0, T.walk (Fin.last nE)} := by
  intro v hv; have := odd_degree_mem_endpoints T v; aesop;

/-
**Euler's parity theorem.**  In any multigraph admitting an Eulerian trail,
at most two vertices have odd degree.
-/
theorem odd_degree_vertices_le_two (T : EulerianTrail G) :
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun v => Odd (degree G v))).card ≤ 2 := by
  exact le_trans ( Finset.card_le_card ( oddVerts_subset T ) ) ( Finset.card_insert_le _ _ )

end EulerianTrailParity

/-!
# Entropy-Complexity Bridge: From Compression to Information Bounds

This file establishes formal bridges between algorithmic compression/complexity
and entropy-like information bounds on finite types. The central theme is:

> **Compression controls entropy-like support complexity.**
> If a finite family of objects can be injectively encoded into a bounded
> code space, then the family's cardinality (and hence its log-cardinality,
> a uniform entropy surrogate) is bounded by the code space size.

## Main Results

### Finite cardinality bounds from injective encodings
- `card_le_of_injective_to_fin`: Injective map to `Fin N` bounds cardinality by `N`.
- `card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code`: Injective map to `Fin (2^k)` bounds cardinality by `2^k`.
- `card_le_two_pow_of_injective_bitcode`: Injective map to `Fin k → Bool` bounds cardinality by `2^k`.
- `card_range_le_two_pow_of_bitlength_bound`: Range of a map to `Fin (2^k)` has size ≤ `2^k`.

### Entropy bounds
- `EntropyBound`: Predicate `Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k`, the finite uniform entropy inequality.
- `entropyBound_of_injective_code`: Injective code implies entropy bound.
- `uniform_entropy_le_code_length`: Log-cardinality bounded by code length.

### Support monotonicity (data processing)
- `support_entropy_monotone_under_map`: `|range f| ≤ |α|`.
- `card_range_le_card_codomain`: `|range f| ≤ |β|`.
- `support_entropy_comp_monotone`: `|range (g ∘ f)| ≤ |range f|` — deterministic data processing.

### Cross-domain bridge
- `complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound`: Connects compressor bounds
  to finite cardinality control.

## Mathematical Significance

These theorems form the combinatorial skeleton of the source coding principle
and create a formal route from Kolmogorov-style complexity bounds to
entropy/information inequalities. The composition monotonicity theorem
`support_entropy_comp_monotone` is a combinatorial shadow of the
**data processing inequality**: deterministic post-processing cannot
increase the number of distinguishable outputs.
-/

open Set Function Finset Fintype

/-! ## Section 1: Core Finite Cardinality Bounds -/

/-- An injective map from a finite type to `Fin N` implies the source has
at most `N` elements. This is the fundamental counting principle underlying
all compression-to-entropy arguments. -/
theorem card_le_of_injective_to_fin
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {N : ℕ}
    (f : α → Fin N) (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ N := by
  calc Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card (Fin N) := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hf
    _ = N := Fintype.card_fin N

/-- An injective encoding into `Fin (2^k)` bounds source cardinality by `2^k`.
This is the exponential form of the entropy bound: if objects can be
described by `k`-bit codes, there are at most `2^k` of them. -/
theorem card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k :=
  card_le_of_injective_to_fin enc henc

/-- The cardinality of the function space `Fin k → Bool` is exactly `2^k`.
This witnesses bitstrings of length `k` as a code space of size `2^k`. -/
theorem fintype_card_fun_bool (k : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card (Fin k → Bool) = 2^k := by
  simp [Fintype.card_fin, Fintype.card_bool]

/-- An injective encoding into explicit bitstrings `Fin k → Bool` bounds
cardinality by `2^k`. This is the most concrete form: each element gets
a unique `k`-bit string, so there can be at most `2^k` elements. -/
theorem card_le_two_pow_of_injective_bitcode
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (f : α → (Fin k → Bool)) (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k := by
  calc Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card (Fin k → Bool) := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hf
    _ = 2^k := fintype_card_fun_bool k

/-- The range of any map into `Fin (2^k)` has at most `2^k` elements.
This does not require injectivity — it bounds the number of distinguishable
outputs of any encoding scheme. -/
theorem card_range_le_two_pow_of_bitlength_bound
    {n k : ℕ} (f : Fin n → Fin (2^k)) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ 2^k := by
  calc Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card (Fin (2^k)) := Fintype.card_subtype_le _
    _ = 2^k := Fintype.card_fin _

/-! ## Section 2: Entropy Bound Predicate and Logarithmic Form -/

/-- `EntropyBound α k` asserts that the uniform entropy of the finite type `α`
is at most `k` bits: equivalently, `|α| ≤ 2^k`. This is the finite
combinatorial skeleton of the source coding bound `H(X) ≤ k` for a
uniform source over `α` encoded with `k`-bit codewords. -/
def EntropyBound (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k

/-- An injective encoding into `k`-bit codes implies the entropy bound.
This is the formal finite-uniform entropy inequality: if every element
of `α` receives a unique `k`-bit code, then `H(α) ≤ k`. -/
theorem entropyBound_of_injective_code
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    EntropyBound α k :=
  card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code enc henc

/-
Logarithmic form of the entropy bound: if `α` injects into `Fin (2^k)`,
then `log₂ |α| ≤ k`. Uses `Nat.log` which is the floor of the logarithm.
-/
theorem uniform_entropy_le_code_length
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Nat.log 2 (Fintype.card α) ≤ k := by
  -- We have card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code which gives Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k.
  -- Taking the base-2 logarithm is monotonic, so log₂ |α| ≤ log₂ 2^k = k.
  have hcard : Fintype.card α ≤ 2 ^ k := by
    apply card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code enc henc
  exact (Nat.log_mono_right hcard).trans (Nat.log_pow (by norm_num : 1 < 2) k).le

/-- For any injective encoding `α → Fin (2^k)`, the
log-cardinality of `α` is bounded by `k`. -/
theorem log_card_range_le_of_embedding_into_bitstrings
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Nat.log 2 (Fintype.card α) ≤ k :=
  uniform_entropy_le_code_length enc henc

/-! ## Section 3: Support Monotonicity — Data Processing -/

/-- The range of a map has at most as many elements as its domain.
This is a combinatorial form of the principle that deterministic
processing cannot create new distinguishable outputs. -/
theorem support_entropy_monotone_under_map
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq β]
    (f : α → β) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card α :=
  Fintype.card_range_le f

/-- The range of a map has at most as many elements as the codomain.
This is the trivial but useful fact that range ⊆ codomain implies
the cardinality inequality. -/
theorem card_range_le_card_codomain
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    (f : α → β) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card β :=
  Fintype.card_subtype_le _

/-
**Combinatorial Data Processing Inequality.**
Composition cannot increase the number of distinguishable outputs:
`|range (g ∘ f)| ≤ |range f|`. This is the finite combinatorial
shadow of the data processing inequality `H(g(X)) ≤ H(X)` for
deterministic channels.
-/
theorem support_entropy_comp_monotone
    {α β γ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
    (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range (g ∘ f)) ≤ Fintype.card (Set.range f) := by
  -- By definition of range, we know that every element in the range of `g ∘ f` is of the form `g (f a)` for some `a ∈ α`.
  have h_range : Set.range (g ∘ f) = g '' Set.range f := by
    grind +splitIndPred;
  simp +decide only [h_range, card_ofFinset];
  refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_image_le ) _;
  exact Finset.card_le_card fun x hx => by aesop;

/-! ## Section 4: Compression Lower Bounds -/

/-
If a type has more than `2^k` elements, no injective encoding into
`k`-bit codes exists. This is the compression impossibility theorem:
you cannot losslessly compress a family of size `> 2^k` into `k` bits.
-/
theorem no_injective_code_of_card_gt
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (hcard : 2^k < Fintype.card α) :
    ¬ ∃ f : α → Fin (2^k), Function.Injective f := by
  exact fun ⟨ f, hf ⟩ => not_le_of_gt hcard ( card_le_of_injective_to_fin f hf )

/-! ## Section 5: Subadditivity Under Products -/

/-
Product encoding: if `α` has at most `2^k` elements and `β` has at most
`2^ℓ` elements, then `α × β` has at most `2^(k + ℓ)` elements.
This is entropy subadditivity: `H(X, Y) ≤ H(X) + H(Y)`.
-/
theorem entropyBound_prod_of_entropyBound
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] {k ℓ : ℕ}
    (hα : EntropyBound α k) (hβ : EntropyBound β ℓ) :
    EntropyBound (α × β) (k + ℓ) := by
  unfold EntropyBound at *;
  simpa only [ pow_add, Fintype.card_prod ] using Nat.mul_le_mul hα hβ

/-! ## Section 6: Cross-Domain Bridge to Compression-Complexity -/

namespace EntropyComplexityBridge

/-- An invertible compressor with idempotence, length-bounding, and inverse. -/
structure InvertibleCompressor where
  compress : List Bool → List Bool
  decompress : List Bool → List Bool
  hidem : ∀ s, compress (compress s) = compress s
  hlen : ∀ s, (compress s).length ≤ s.length
  hstrict : ∀ s, compress s ≠ s → (compress s).length < s.length
  hinv : ∀ s, decompress (compress s) = s

/-
**Complexity bound implies finite entropy bound (bridge theorem).**

Given an invertible compressor `C` and a finite family of binary strings,
if every element has compressed length ≤ `k`, then the family has at most
`2^(k+1)` elements (since there are `2^(k+1) - 1` binary strings of
length ≤ `k`).

This is the key bridge: algorithmic complexity upper bounds (via compressors)
imply entropy upper bounds (via cardinality control).
-/
theorem complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound
    (C : InvertibleCompressor)
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (embed : α → List Bool)
    (hembed : Function.Injective embed)
    {k : ℕ}
    (hbound : ∀ a : α, (C.compress (embed a)).length ≤ k) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^(k+1) := by
  -- We know that `compress` is injective and its image is contained in the set of lists of length ≤ k.
  have h_image : Finset.card (Finset.image (fun a => C.compress (embed a)) Finset.univ) ≤ 2^(k+1) - 1 := by
    -- The set of lists of length ≤ k is finite and has cardinality 2^(k+1) - 1.
    have h_card : Finset.card (Finset.filter (fun l => l.length ≤ k) (Finset.biUnion (Finset.range (k + 1)) (fun i => Finset.image (fun l : Fin i → Bool => List.ofFn l) (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin i → Bool)))) ) ≤ 2^(k+1) - 1 := by
      refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_filter_le _ _ ) _;
      refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_biUnion_le ) _;
      rw [ Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i hi => Finset.card_image_of_injective _ fun x y hxy => by simpa [ funext_iff ] using hxy ] ; simp +decide [ Nat.geomSum_eq ];
    refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_le_card _ ) h_card;
    simp +decide [ Finset.subset_iff ];
    exact fun a => ⟨ ⟨ _, hbound a, fun i => ( C.compress ( embed a ) |> List.get <| ⟨ i, by linarith [ hbound a, i.2 ] ⟩ ), by simp +decide ⟩, hbound a ⟩;
  rw [ Finset.card_image_of_injective _ fun a b hab => hembed <| by have := C.hinv ( embed a ) ; have := C.hinv ( embed b ) ; aesop ] at h_image ; exact le_trans h_image ( Nat.sub_le _ _ )

/-- **Finite family complexity certificate.**
If a compressor certifies that every element of a finite type has
compressed representation of length ≤ `k`, this yields an entropy
bound on the type. -/
theorem entropyBound_of_compressor
    (C : InvertibleCompressor)
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (embed : α → List Bool)
    (hembed : Function.Injective embed)
    {k : ℕ}
    (hbound : ∀ a : α, (C.compress (embed a)).length ≤ k) :
    EntropyBound α (k + 1) :=
  complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound C embed hembed hbound

end EntropyComplexityBridge
